# Cueflick — authoring guide for AI agents

For any AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, and others).

Cueflick plays "product films" for software: video-like films of a workflow moving across
app screens, with a directed camera and motion-graphics characters. You write one JSON file
(a clip); the library plays it. You never write animation code, CSS, or HTML.

Part 1 is the format. Part 2 is how to direct a good film. Part 3 is how to add a screen
type when the app you need isn't built in.

## Your loop

1. Read this guide. Run `npx cueflick catalog` to see templates, surfaces, parts, and actions.
2. Write `<name>.clip.json`. Start from `npx cueflick init` if there is no clip yet.
3. Run `npx cueflick validate <file>`. Fix every ✗ error. Each line gives a JSON path, the
   problem, and usually a hint ("Did you mean …?"). Treat ! warnings as likely mistakes too
   (typos in keys, steps in the wrong order, acting on a screen or actor that is off stage).
4. Run `npx cueflick snapshot <file>`. Open every PNG and check: nothing cut off, text
   readable, the action in frame, the story clear chapter by chapter. Fix and repeat.
5. Share it: `npx cueflick export <file>` (one self-contained .html) or
   `npx cueflick render <file> --out film.mp4` (video), or embed with <cue-flick src="...">.

# Part 1 — the format

## File anatomy

{
  "cueflick": "1",
  "title": "Short film title",
  "template": "assistant-files" | "phone-feature" | "assistant-connector" | "trigger-automation-notify",
  "layout": "row" | "stage" | "desktop",        (optional; the template has a default)
  "disclaimer": "Illustration · names and records are made up",
  "story":   { "overview", "description", "audience", "workflow": [ ... ] },
  "design":  { "mode", "aspect", "accent", "font", "radius", "camera", "pace", "cursor", "backdrop" },
  "screens": { "<id>": { "surface": "...", "app": { "name", "color", "icon" }, ... } },
  "actors":  { "<id>": { "shape": "sphere", "color": "#ffc83d", ... } },          (optional)
  "chapters": [ { "title", "narration", "focus", "zoom", "duration", "ease", "async", "backdrop", "steps": [ ... ] } ]
}

- story.overview (required): one or two sentences — what happens and why it matters.
- story.workflow: the process as plain sentences; shown on the end card.
- chapters[].narration: the script line for that chapter, shown as the subtitle. One sentence.
- chapters[].backdrop: the stage colour for this scene ("#hex", or ["#top", "#bottom"]).

## Screens: placement and visibility

Every screen also accepts:
- "mode": "light" | "dark"   this screen's colours, whatever design.mode is (mix them freely)
- "hidden": true             start off stage; bring it on with { "enter": "<id>" }
- "place": a slot ("left", "center", "right", "wide-left", "wide-right", "full", "pip", "pip-left")
           or { "x", "y", "w", "h" } in world units (the world is 1600×900)
- "width": world units

Layouts: row = side by side · stage = one large screen at a time (use enter/exit) ·
desktop = overlapping windows (use front to raise one and dim the rest).

## Targets

A target is a screen id ("crm"), "screen.part:name", an actor id ("sunny"), or one piece of
an actor group ("tiles.piece:2"):
  crm.field:Stage   flow.node:trigger   chat.file:q3-chart   chat.area:composer   phone.row:sunny
Use "all" in focus to frame everything on stage (screens and actors).

## Templates

assistant-files (stage) — Someone asks an AI assistant about their own files, pulling them in
  with "@" while typing; a hover previews each file; the reply cites its sources. Needs ai-chat
  with "files". Chapters: type with @references → hover to check → send → read and answer → hover a cited source.

phone-feature (stage) — A phone feature told in a motion-graphics style: actors carry the story
  between scenes, there's no pointer, and confetti finishes it. Needs phone. Chapters: hook with
  actors → the problem on the phone → the feature (ask Iris / summarize / pool / a list) → the payoff as blocks → regroup and finish.

assistant-connector (stage) — An AI assistant uses a connector to do a job in another app.
  Needs ai-chat (plus the target app, often browser-app with "hidden": true).
  Chapters: connect → ask → tool calls + reply → { "enter": app } and show the result → recap.

trigger-automation-notify (row) — A record changes in one app, an automation runs, a team is
  notified in chat. Needs crm-record, flow-canvas, team-chat.

## Surfaces

ai-chat (an AI assistant)
  assistant?, model?, user?, title?, greeting?, placeholder?, recents[]?,
  look?: "warm" (soft, serif, like Claw) | "neutral" (plain grey, sans-serif, like GossipT)
  connectors?: [ { id, name, app? (screen id), icon?, color?, enabled? } ]
  files?: [ { id, name, kind?: image|doc|pdf|sheet, meta?, src?, preview? } ]
    src: a real image (https URL, a path in the clip's folder, or data:image/...); otherwise
    preview draws one: { title?, chart?: [numbers], lines?: [text], rows?: [[cells]], color? }
  parts: connector, file, area (composer | thread | sidebar)
  steps: { "connect": "chat.connector:books" }
         { "prompt": "Does @q3-chart back up @board-memo?", "draft": true }   "@id" pulls a file in; draft leaves it unsent
         { "send": true }
         { "hover": "chat.file:q3-chart", "zoom": true, "ms": 1500 }   pops the preview up; zoom moves the camera in
         { "think": 1200 }
         { "tool": "read_file", "connector": "books", "input": { ... }, "result": "...", "ms": 900 }
         { "respond": "Mostly, yes. @q3-chart shows *21%* growth.\n- a bullet" }

phone (a frameless phone: lock screen or an app list)
  time?, date?, assistant? ("Iris"), material?: glass | light | dark, wallpaper?: [1–3 hex],
  corner? (24–60 px), poolInset? (4–16 px), glow?: [2–7 hex], notifications?: [ ... ],
  screen?: "lock" | "list", list?: { title, circles?: [hex], sections: [ { title?, rows: [
      { id, label, icon?, color?, detail?, value?, toggle?: bool, chevron?: bool } ] } ] }
  parts: note, row, area (pool | clock | notes | summary | ask | list)
  steps: { "notify": { "id": "sam", "app": "Messages", "icon": "💬", "color": "#34c759", "title": "Sam", "text": "...", "time": "2m ago" } }
         { "ask": "What did I miss?" }            the edge glows; the request is written out
         { "summarize": "Sam moved dinner to 8…", "title": "4 notifications" }   folds the pile into one card
         { "pool": "music", "title": "Night Drive", "artist": "Mira Sol", "art": ["#ff7a59", "#7b2ff7"], "expand": true }
         { "pool": "iris" } (listening)   { "pool": "idle" }
         { "toggle": "phone.row:summaries" }   { "tap": "phone.row:sunny" }   (list screens; a touch ripple, no pointer)
  The Screen Pool's corners always follow the screen's: radius = corner − poolInset.

crm-record
  record: { title, fields{}, module?, type?, stages[]?, stageField? ("Stage"), options{}?, buttons[]?, activity[]? }
  parts: field, button
  steps: { "choose": "crm.field:Stage", "value": "Closed Won" }   { "type": "crm.field:Notes", "text": "..." }
         { "click": "crm.button:Save" }   { "toast": "Opportunity saved" }

flow-canvas (a node-based automation editor)
  workflow?, nodes: [ { id, title, sub?, icon?, color?, app? (screen id), trigger?, params{}? } ]  2–6 nodes
  parts: node
  steps: { "run": "flow.node:trigger", "ms": 12, "output": { ... }, "result": "true" }   run nodes in order
         { "open": "flow.node:format" }   { "expression": "{{ $json.name }} closed", "preview": "Acme closed", "field": "Message" }

team-chat
  channel, channels[]?, workspace?, members?, history[]? ({ from, text, time? })
  steps: { "message": { "app": "flow", "text": "🎉 *Bold* and `code`" } }   { "react": { "emoji": "🎉", "count": 3 } }
         { "reply": { "from": "Maya Chen", "text": "Great work!" } }

browser-app (a web app in a browser window: header, side nav, summary cards, a table)
  url?, tab?, company?, title?, nav[]?, active?, summary[]? ({ label, value, tone? }),
  columns[], rows: [ { id, cells[], status?, tone?, new?, detail{}? } ]   tone: ok | warn | danger | info | muted
  parts: row
  steps: { "add": "books.row:1042" }   { "status": "books.row:1042", "to": "Paid" }   { "select": "books.row:1042" }   { "toast": "..." }

When two screens support the same action (e.g. "toast"), add "on": "<screen id>".

## Actors (characters)

"actors": { "sunny": { "shape": "sphere", "color": "#ffc83d", "size": 120, "at": { "x": 690, "y": 400 } } }
  shape: sphere | block | pill | ring · size: 16–600 world units · at: start point (world is 1600×900)
  finish: gloss (default) | matte | glass · squash: 0–2 (how soft it is; spheres 1, blocks 0.4)
  groups: count (1–24), columns, gap, colors: [per piece], labels: [per piece] — e.g. a row of labelled blocks
Steps:
  { "spawn": ["sunny", "coral"], "effect": "pop" | "drop" | "rise" | "fade", "stagger": 140, "at": <spot> }
  { "move": "sunny", "to": <spot>, "path": "hop" | "bounce" | "roll" | "slide" | "float",
    "perch": true, "offset": { "x": -88, "y": 0 }, "height": 200, "bounces": 2, "bounciness": 0.36,
    "duration": 900, "ease": "spring", "async": true }
  { "leave": "sunny", "effect": "pop" | "fall" | "shrink" | "fade" }
  { "confetti": <spot>, "count": 140 }
  <spot> = a target (with "perch": true it sits on top of it) or a world point { "x", "y" }.
  hop arcs and squashes on landing; bounce rebounds ("bounces" times, each "bounciness" as high);
  roll stays on the surface and turns as it goes; a new move on an actor takes over smoothly.

## Camera and motion

Chapter: "focus" (a target or "all"), "zoom", "duration" (ms), "ease", "async": true (steps start
while the camera still moves). Design camera: { zoom: 1–2.5, speed: 0.25–3, ease, follow: true, punch }.
  ease: smooth | snappy | linear | gentle | spring
  follow: the camera eases toward what each step acts on, and keeps a caret in view while typing.
  punch: true | 1.3 | { amount, hold }: a quick zoom toward each click (a step can say "punch": false).
Steps for any film:
  { "focus": "chat.area:composer", "zoom": 1.4, "duration": 900, "ease": "gentle", "async": true }
  { "pan": "books.row:1042" } or { "pan": { "x": 300, "y": 0 } }
  { "dive": "coral", "into": "#06352f" }   zoom through a target until it fills the frame (change scene behind it)
  { "blur": "phone", "amount": 7 }         keep one screen or actor sharp, blur the rest; { "blur": false } clears
  { "backdrop": "#ffffff" }                change the stage colour now
  { "caption": "..." }  { "wait": 1200 }   { "packet": { "from": "crm", "to": "flow.node:trigger" } }
  { "enter": "books", "from": "right" }    from: left | right | top | bottom | fade | zoom | pop | drop | launch | flip
  { "exit": "claw", "to": "minimize" }      to: the same, plus minimize
  { "front": "books", "dim": true }

## Design

mode: dark | light | auto · aspect: auto | 16:9 | 4:5 | 1:1 (auto goes portrait on phones) ·
accent: hex · font: { ui, mono } · radius: 0–24 · camera (above) · pace: 0.25–3 ·
cursor: false (touch-first films hide the pointer) · backdrop: "#hex" or ["#top", "#bottom"] ·
intro / subtitles / endcard: booleans (default true).

# Part 2 — directing a good film

A film is a sequence of beats. A beat is one new thing the viewer notices. Aim for a beat every
1.5–3 seconds, 3–6 chapters, 30–60 seconds in all.

## Shape the story

1. Hook (one chapter): something visual and simple before any UI — characters popping in, a
   screen arriving. No explanation yet.
2. The problem (one chapter): show the pain in the product: the pile of notifications, the
   copy-paste, the long form.
3. The feature (one or two chapters): the product doing the job, step by step, in its own UI.
4. The payoff (one chapter): the result, made tangible — blocks with labels, a row marked
   "Sent", a message to the team.
5. Close: regroup, a recap ("focus": "all"), or confetti. The end card shows story.workflow.

## Camera grammar

- Open wide, push in for detail, pull back for context. One camera move per beat.
- Frame the thing that changes, not the whole app: "chat.area:composer", "phone.area:pool".
- Typing: follow on, zoom 1.3–1.6 on the composer. Hover previews: "zoom": true.
- Clicks in a desktop app: punch for a screen-recording feel; skip it for calm, premium films.
- Scene change through an object: end on a character or card, { "dive": "<it>", "into": "<next colour>" },
  then start the next chapter with a focus that pulls back out.
- Isolate one thing: { "blur": "<screen or actor>" } for a beat, then { "blur": false }.
- Use "async": true so the camera arrives while the action starts; never make the viewer wait for it.

## Characters

- Give each one a meaning: a person, a notification, an item. Keep to 3–6.
- Let them carry the viewer between scenes: end a scene with a character alone, start the next
  around it; or dive through it.
- Perch them on what matters (a card, a row, the top of a phone); roll them along an edge to lead the eye.
- Bounce and squash read as "landed"; one or two bounces is plenty.
- Regroup them at the end; that's the visual "it all comes together".

## Mood → settings

| Mood | Settings |
|---|---|
| Playful, consumer | ease spring · bounces 2–3, bounciness 0.45 · squash 1.3–1.6 · gloss · confetti 180+ |
| Premium, calm | ease gentle · speed 0.8 · pace 0.9 · bounces 1 · squash 0.6 · glass · white or soft backdrops |
| Productivity, crisp | ease snappy · follow + punch · async chapters · few or no characters |
| Enterprise, serious | ease smooth · no bounces · matte · one consistent backdrop · no confetti |

## Which template fits the idea

| The idea | Template | Screens |
|---|---|---|
| An AI assistant working with your files | assistant-files | ai-chat (neutral look, files) |
| An AI assistant acting in another app | assistant-connector | ai-chat + browser-app |
| A phone or consumer feature, told with motion | phone-feature | phone + actors |
| A record change that triggers automation and notifies a team | trigger-automation-notify | crm-record + flow-canvas + team-chat |
| An app that isn't built in | register a new screen type (Part 3) | yours |

## Before you finish

- Every chapter's narration says what the viewer sees, in one sentence.
- Snapshots: the subject of each chapter is in frame and readable; nothing important is cut off.
- Every product, person, and number is invented, and the disclaimer says so. Never use real logos.
- Show code and expressions in the product's real syntax (e.g. {{ $json.field }}).
- Clip text is always displayed as text; HTML in a clip is shown literally, never run.

# Part 3 — adding a screen type

When the app you need isn't built in, register a surface before the film loads:

  import { registerSurface, h } from 'cueflick';

  registerSurface({
    name: 'kanban',                          // used as "surface": "kanban"
    summary: 'A kanban board: cards move between columns.',
    width: 520,                              // default width in world units
    keys: ['columns'],                       // screen keys it reads (others are warned about)
    styles: '.kb-col { … }',                 // CSS, scoped to the film's shadow root
    parts: { card: def => def.columns.flatMap(c => c.cards.map(card => card.id)) },
    validate(def, path, report) { /* report.error(path, message, hint) / report.warn(...) */ },
    render(def) {
      const el = h('div', { class: 'cf-window kb' }, /* build with h(); text only */);
      return { el, find: (part, name) => /* the element for "board.card:name" */ null };
    },
    actions: {
      move: {
        summary: 'Move a card to a column: { "move": "board.card:42", "to": "Done" }.',
        part: 'card', keys: ['to'],
        validate(step, def, path, report) {},
        async run(view, step, ctx) {
          // ctx.wait(ms), ctx.animate(ms, t => …), ctx.cursor.moveTo(el, ctx), ctx.cursor.click(ctx),
          // ctx.camera.look(el, { zoom }) / ctx.camera.back() / ctx.camera.track(el), ctx.fast (skip animation)
        }
      }
    }
  });

Rules: build DOM only with h() / s() (text only; no innerHTML, no event-handler attributes);
every wait goes through ctx so pause, pace, and seeking work; handle ctx.fast by jumping to the
end state. For complete examples, read browser-app.js (a small surface) and phone.js (parts, list
rows, the touch ripple) in https://github.com/priyabratasahoo21/cueflick/tree/main/src/surfaces.
